description: Tier 2 diagnostic. What is on the network, and what does ISE know about it? Inventory and classification first, then composition, then the network devices and their activity.

panels.description: Total endpoints in the ISE endpoint database. This is the inventory count, not the live session count — the difference between the two is the estate that is currently switched off.

defaults.noValue: no data — stale, see Collection pipeline

targets.expr: (ise3_endpoints_total) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="endpoint_inventory"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="endpoint_inventory"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="endpoint_inventory"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="endpoint_inventory"} == 1))) == 1))

panels.title: Endpoints

panels.description: Endpoints ISE has not managed to profile. These fall through profile-based authorization rules, so a growing number here usually shows up later as unexpected policy matches.

defaults.noValue: no data — stale, see Collection pipeline

targets.expr: (ise3_endpoints_unprofiled) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="endpoint_inventory"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="endpoint_inventory"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="endpoint_inventory"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="endpoint_inventory"} == 1))) == 1))

panels.title: Unprofiled endpoints

panels.description: Network devices configured in ISE. Compare against the silent device count below: configured but never authenticating is either decommissioned kit or a device that cannot reach ISE.

defaults.noValue: no data — stale, see Collection pipeline

targets.expr: (ise3_network_devices_total) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="network_devices"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="network_devices"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="network_devices"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="network_devices"} == 1))) == 1))

panels.title: Network devices

panels.description: Share of network devices carrying the location, type and owner attributes the rest of this dashboard set groups by. Low classification is why breakdowns elsewhere show large 'unknown' buckets.

defaults.noValue: no data — stale, see Collection pipeline

targets.expr: ((ise3_network_devices_classified) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="network_devices"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="network_devices"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="network_devices"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="network_devices"} == 1))) == 1))) / clamp_min(((ise3_network_devices_total) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="network_devices"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="network_devices"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="network_devices"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="network_devices"} == 1))) == 1))), 1)

panels.description: Share of this dashboard's own datasets that both collected successfully and are inside their freshness window (endpoint_inventory, nad_health, network_devices). Below 100% means some panel here is blank or stale, and the pipeline dashboard says which.

targets.expr: avg(((max by (dataset) (ise3_dataset_up{dataset=~"endpoint_inventory|network_devices|nad_health"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset=~"endpoint_inventory|network_devices|nad_health"} == 1))) == bool 1) * ((max by (dataset) (ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset=~"endpoint_inventory|network_devices|nad_health"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset=~"endpoint_inventory|network_devices|nad_health"} == 1))) == bool 1))

panels.title: Network device detail-cache coverage

panels.description: Purpose, reading order, and where to go next. Kept with the dashboard so the meaning cannot drift away from the panels.

options.content:
**Purpose** — describe what is on the network and what ISE knows about it — the inventory view, not the incident view.

**Read it in this order**

1. Read the inventory counts and the classification share.
2. Use the composition tables to check the estate matches expectation.
3. Work the silent-device list: silence produces no errors anywhere else, so this is the only panel that surfaces it.

**When something is red**

- Low classification: fix the network device attributes in ISE — several dashboards group by them.
- Growing unprofiled count: check the profiling feed before changing policy.
- Blank attribute panels: the detail cache is still filling, see the coverage panel.

**Related dashboards** — Triage, RADIUS access, Posture, Capacity

*Owner: set this to the team that answers the page. Runbook: link it here — a red panel with no runbook is a puzzle, not an alert.*
